title: Digital dental impression (scanner)
what: The doctor moves a small scanner around your mouth and gets a 3D model of your teeth on the screen. No impression putty is needed.
why: For crowns, veneers, inlays, implants, clear aligners and braces, and night guards.
duration: usually 5 to 20 minutes; the model appears right away
tell_doctor: If you have a strong gag reflex
If your jaw hurts or it is hard to keep your mouth open for long
If you have dentures or braces

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: Brush your teeth before the visit.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You can eat beforehand. No special prep is needed.

bring: A referral from your doctor, if you have one
steps: You sit in the dental chair
Your teeth are dried with air
The doctor moves the scanner along your upper and lower teeth
You are asked to bite together to record your bite
The model is checked on screen, and some areas are scanned again if needed
feel: The scanner may feel slightly warm
You need to keep your mouth open for a few minutes
after: You can eat and drink right away
The model is sent to the lab or used for your treatment plan
The doctor will tell you how long it takes to make your item

faq.q: Is it more accurate than a regular impression?
faq.a: Usually it is just as good, and for many types of work more accurate. Your doctor decides.
No. The scanner uses light, like a camera.

reminders.text: Digital teeth scan tomorrow. Brush your teeth before the visit.
